title: Albatwitch Day, celebrating Central Pa.'s very own cryptid, is back for 2026

COLUMBIA/WRIGHTSVILLE, Pa. (WHTM) -- Did you know there was a small, hairy creature eerily similar to Bigfoot that is said to have been roaming both Lancaster and York counties for decades?

Well, you do now.

Central Pennsylvania's very own cryptid, the Albatwitch, is "a 3-to-5-foot-tall creature" with "a skinny frame, dark hair and glowing yellow eyes," known to steal apples, which gave it the Pennsylvania Dutch name for "apple snitch."

The Columbia Historic Preservation Society has held an annual festival in honor of the Albatwitch since 2014, moving the event to Wrightsville last year. It'll be back again for its "unlucky 13th edition" on Saturday, Oct. 10, at Riverfront Park, starting at 11 a.m. and running until 6 p.m.

Special guests include Weird N.J. Magazine founder and TV star Mark Moran (History Channel, Discovery and Travel Channel), Sarah Cooper of the American Snallygaster Museum (another United States cryptid), author and former Marine Daniel P. Glick, cryptid research author David Hardie, and Dan and Will Wilson.

Art and merchandise will be available for sale, along with food and drinks. There will also be musical performances by a trio of Pennsylvania artists: Dillweed, Swamp Whompers and Logan & Aliccia. Lancaster Stormers mascot Cylo will also make a special guest appearance alongside an Albatwitch mascot.

The day's schedule will conclude with Albatwitch Haunted Trolley Tours of Wrightsville, with 48-person tours scheduled for 7 and 9 p.m. For more information, go to albatwitchday.com.
